description: AccessPay is a fintech business that works with enterprise customers, integrating their accounting software and back-office systems with their banks. Using AccessPay, businesses can reduce manual data entry and improve overall cash management and control, safeguarding their transactions and automating functions for a more efficient finance operation.
why_backed: AccessPay is a business we had followed for some time prior to our investment. It has a very impressive cap table, which includes both Mastercard and NatWest. In addition, the business is led by a very backable founder and CEO in Anish Kapoor, who previously founded Telecity ahead of exiting it two years after a £436m IPO. Anish also founded YuuGuu – a desktop sharing and web conferencing application bought by PowWowNow.

description: AeroCloud has created a SaaS-based operating system for commercial and general airports, providing everything from flight tracking, gate management and lease management to tickets, anonymised customer tracking and flight information boards. To date, the business has focused on the secondary airport market, which is greatly underserved and accounts for 3000 airports in the US and Europe.
why_backed: AeroCloud is backed by a first-rate management team with prior aviation and global operational experience. The business also reached $2m ARR within two years of commercialisation, counting airports in Manchester, Eindhoven, Tampa, and Orange County as clients. AeroCloud also has a large addressable market, where Microsoft Excel is its main competitor in the secondary airport space.

description: Arctic Shores specialises in psychometric online job assessments which are used to help employers hire staff without risk of unconscious bias. Potential hires take an assessment as part of the interview process. This assesses a candidate’s soft skills and their fit for a job, helping employers to make the right decision when hiring.
why_backed: Right now employers are facing a significant skills shortage and having to select candidates from a limited talent pool. To help employers overcome these challenges, Arctic Shores is using its platform to unearth quality candidates who may be overlooked in the traditional CV process, which it describes as outdated. The team has already supported major names such as Vitality, PwC and TalkTalk.

description: Atomik AM creates sustainable materials and patented technologies to support scalable and efficient advanced manufacturing, such as a Universal Binder – or glue – to supercharge 3D printing across automotive, aerospace and energy. The company prides itself on a materials-first, solutions focused approach that takes a holistic approach to advanced manufacturing instead of solving individual problems.
why_backed: Atomik AM’s founder Professor Kate Black is highly backable, credible and respected in this field, having previously exited a similar business she founded prior to starting Atomik. Kate’s enthusiasm and unwavering commitment to sustainability is both authentic and in-demand among the major businesses she works with, with corporates across the board investing to reduce their carbon footprint and meet their ESG targets.

description: Audiebant specialises in mass communications solutions which can be used to issue vital information or critical alerts to ensure public safety. For example, during an act of terrorism or extreme weather. Audiebant can deliver communications via audio networks, mobiles, PCs and outdoor tech (including digital displays).
why_backed: Audiebant has displayed excellent traction, expanding across the UK, Europe and US. Its clients include governments, schools and companies across the corporate and leisure sectors. Audiebant expects its business to grow even further, following new legislation (Martyn’s Law) that will put a greater onus on events and venues around safety protocols with regards to terrorism and emergencies, following the 2017 Manchester Arena attack.

description: BankiFi is a fintech company that aims to alleviate the common headaches SMEs face when operating a business. Its platform, which is sold to banks to help them better service SMEs, rolls invoicing, payments, collections, accounting and tax into one.
why_backed: BankiFi’s founder, Mark Hartley, is well known in fintech. Before BankiFi, he helped scale and exit Clear2Pay for €375m. Mark is also highly experienced in selling to banks and has an incredible network to help scale BankiFi, including FIS and Visa.

description: BlueSkeye AI is leading advancements in the digital health and wellbeing space through artificial intelligence and machine learning. Through its expertise, the company is making it easier to detect and diagnose mental health conditions and enhance people’s wellbeing.
why_backed: Founder Michel Valstar spent 15 years developing his award-winning company. A world-leader in his field, he has also been published in over 100 journals. In addition, the scope of BlueSkeye AI’s tech is far-reaching, with use cases across the health and automotive sectors, where legislative focus around driver and passenger safety is increasing.

description: BOW (Bettering our Worlds), which originally spun out from the University of Sheffield in 2020, offers a software platform that simplifies robotics development. BOW’s ‘robot-agnostic’ software development kit bridges diverse robotic systems, enabling seamless integration across platforms and operating systems.
why_backed: BOW’s ‘robot-agnostic’ software development kit (SDK) addresses the complexity and cost of programming robots, enabling seamless integration across diverse systems. With the robotics market projected to reach $260 billion by 2030, BOW’s collaborative approach positions them to significantly impact the industry. At the time of our investment, Raspberry-Pi Co-Founder Liz Upton is also Chair of the Board, further strengthening the company’s leadership.

description: CareLoop is a digital therapeutic platform and University of Manchester spinout that focuses on tackling severe mental illness. Launched in 2021, the platform integrates with existing treatment pathways, providing digital support and enabling clinicians to monitor patients remotely. The company was founded by mental health academics and is led by CEO Zoë Blake, who previously delivered 10x growth at the digital mental health platform Kooth plc.
why_backed: We invested in CareLoop because we understood their mission and vision for transforming severe mental illness aftercare from our first meeting. The business is doing innovative work within the severe mental illness space, is backed by over a decade of clinical research, and exemplifies the quality of spinouts from the University of Manchester and North West universities in general.

description: CloudGuard is a cybersecurity company that has created a comprehensive AI-powered platform to provide companies with enhanced protection from threats. The company helps clients to respond to cybersecurity concerns with tools for threat intelligence, static analysis, and dynamic analytics. Founded in 2020, CloudGuard’s mission is to improve security across cloud environments and offer solutions for vulnerability management, risk assessment, and incident response.
why_backed: We invested in CloudGuard after being impressed by the company’s experienced founding team, which has successfully scaled and exited previous start-ups, as well as its deep technical and commercial expertise, particularly in the Microsoft ecosystem. The company operates in a highly acquisitive sector with strong M&A activity and high EBITDA multiples. Additionally, CloudGuard has demonstrated impressive growth and has a strong pipeline of potential customers.

description: Coadjute connects all parties within a property transaction via its innovative blockchain network, making the process of transacting a property faster and more efficient. Capitalising on the growing demand for proptech, Coadjute’s real-time property updates reduce the need for parties within a transaction to chase stakeholders.
why_backed: Coadjute’s solution holds plenty of potential for a property market that’s quickly adapting. Rather than disrupting the market, Coadjute works with existing tech, making adoption easier. As well as being impressed by the tech, Coadjute’s management team and vision also played a key role in our decision to invest.

description: Covatic works with media companies and broadcasters to deliver targeted advertising and marketing solutions that don’t expose users’ personal data. The company works closely with Comcast, an investor in the business and the owner of Sky, NBC and AT&T, having been through the company’s accelerator programme in 2021.
why_backed: Covatic’s technology is cutting edge and perfectly balances advertising effectiveness with data protection and security. In addition, the market for personalised advertising is enormous and the trend of advertisers moving away from cookie-based targeting technology continues to gain pace, as evidenced by the major brands already working with Covatic.

description: Culture Shift is a groundbreaking platform that is working to end bullying and harassment in the workplace and in the classroom. Through anonymous, real-time reporting, Culture Shift is helping more people feel safer at work and during study.
why_backed: Culture Shift has endless potential as a force for good. As well as securing contracts with universities around the country, the business continues to generate new pipeline leads via the health and public sectors, increasing its ARR significantly.

description: Cyclr specialises in embedding integrations (iPaaS) into the SaaS companies it supports, enabling SaaS companies to connect customer data with third-party tools and software. By handling and maintaining integrations, Cyclr’s essential work takes the burden off a company’s developers, so they can focus on revenue driving activities instead.
why_backed: SaaS businesses depend on integrations, which makes Cyclr’s revenue very sticky. In addition, the iPaaS sector is now booming, with Cyclr boasting a strong addressable market. As well as having a very backable management team, our decision to invest was driven by the fact Cyclr is accelerating in all areas, with a pipeline and commercial strategy that we believe will see its growth continue.

description: Cytix provides specialist cybersecurity services to companies by identifying high risk vulnerabilities during code development. By providing an alternative solution to most automated testing, Cytix is able to spot threats earlier and catch vulnerabilities that can be missed by companies and their cybersecurity partners.
why_backed: Cytix demonstrated many positive indicators at the time of our investment alongside clear plans for the future. The founding team had also worked together for eight years and have created a platform that creates collaboration between security and development teams, which has significant benefits as the demand for sophisticated cybersecurity grows.

description: Decently is the company behind the healthcare platform Melo, which enables clinicians and hospital staff to track patient behaviour on brain trauma wards to prevent adverse episodes. Melo’s main focus is patients recovering from an acquired brain injury, which relates to non-birth related trauma – e.g., as a result of being in a coma.
why_backed: Decently replaces largely manual forms of data capture, which is time-consuming and a burden on stretched healthcare staff, with an easy-to-use dashboard and tools. What led us to invest was Decently’s impressive management team and the fact the company is addressing an unmet need. In addition, at the time of investment, Decently had pilots in the Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust and Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.

description: EarSwitch is an innovative medtech company specialising in in-ear biometric sensor technology. The company’s key proposition, EarMetrics®, provides clinicians with credible, real-world health data that’s racially inclusive and non-intrusive. EarMetrics® can be integrated into wearables, hearing aids and hand-held diagnostic health devices.
why_backed: EarSwitch’s mission is to transform healthcare, including how conditions are diagnosed. The company’s technology is highly impressive, and the business itself is one of eight selected to join the UK Government’s Innovative Devices Access Pathway (IDAP) pilot scheme. This is a collaboration between the National institute for Health and Care Excellence, NHS England and the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency to accelerate ground-breaking medical devices.

description: Enthuse is the UK’s second-largest charity fundraising platform behind JustGiving, raising over £100m for charity. Enthuse encourages repeat donations by inspiring direct relationships between supporters and each charity – not the donation brand.
why_backed: Enthuse has rapidly grown to become the no.2 player in the charitable donations space, presenting an opportunity to win even more market share in the UK and grow overseas. All of this combined makes Enthuse an attractive acquisition target.

description: Exciting Instruments is a pioneering deep tech company that has developed a practical and efficient platform for single-molecule detection. This technology allows users to visualise and analyse individual molecules and their interactions, providing high throughput processing and automation of analytics. Their platform is transforming drug development, clinical diagnostics, and research applications across pharma, healthcare, and industrial sectors.
why_backed: Exciting Instruments’ innovative platform addresses the complexities and limited accessibility of single-molecule microscopy, driving new discoveries in drug development and clinical diagnostics. Their vision to bring single-molecule detection to every lab globally and their strong leadership make them a compelling investment for transforming global health outcomes.

description: Feedstock’s highly intuitive Client Relationship Analytics system (CRA) rivals manual CRM tools by going deeper to help businesses monitor and sustain valuable client relationships. With CRA, businesses have better access to crucial insights.
why_backed: Global financial firms and brands in diverse sectors are utilising Feedstock’s intelligent services. An experienced board is also helping Feedstock unlock new opportunities in an area of digital where the demand for in-depth data is only growing.

description: Fluid.work’s all-in-one business management tool addresses the disconnect between teams and processes that use multiple work management programs by bringing everything together in one solution. Combining visual dashboards with intuitive integration, Fluid.work’s mission is to tackle unproductive meetings, unclear communications and automate time consuming tasks, freeing up more time for teams that use Fluid.work.
why_backed: As well as being impressed by Fluid.work’s management team, we felt the company has developed a mature product in a market that’s well-established and growing. The company has won significant global clients, such as Herbalife, Investec, Santander and Walmart. A human-supported SaaS approach also sets Fluid.work apart from its competitors, with significant resource dedicated to account management and onboarding.

description: Futr’s mission is to deliver superpowers to critical service teams. From intelligent self-serve chatbots to making live chat agents instantly multilingual in over 100 languages, Futr is transforming the way organisations serve their audiences.
why_backed: Futr’s leading natural language platform is gaining traction in social housing, retail, university, government, charity and the police, where it’s speeding up response times. Futr is also helping suicide charity CALM save lives with 24/7 support.

description: HURR is an online fashion rental platform that combines a peer-to-peer marketplace with a while label SaaS solution centred around enabling consumers to rent high fashion garments. HURR is partnered with a number of major retailers including, Net-A-Porter and John Lewis, and powers 130+ top brands, including renowned names such as Ganni and Mulberry.
why_backed: HURR’s highly backable founder Victoria Prew describes the company as the next-big-thing in fashion, and there is plenty of evidence to back this up, with celebrity endorsements and a 4.7 Truspilot rating from 12k reviews. Along with the rising demand for fashion rental solutions among consumers, HURR is very sustainability-focused, bucking the trend of fast fashion with quality pieces that can be worn and enjoyed time and again.

description: Illuma has created a highly innovative contextual advertising platform that enables advertisers to target specific audiences without the use of cookies, enabling the world’s biggest brands to maximise their ROI and make better ad placement decisions in real-time.
why_backed: Trusted by global brands such as Sky, VW and Coca-Cola, Illuma’s technology enables advertisers to consider sophisticated details like article sentiment and reader mindset before placing ads. This is an industry first that is hugely valuable amid plans to phase out cookies.

description: Inotec has created an award-winning medical treatment called NATROX® Oxygen Wound Therapy, which uses a small wearable device to heal complex wounds. Early success has also led the Cambridge company to open its first NATROX® clinic in Kuala Lumpur.
why_backed: Inotec’s best-in-class device is backed by founders who have exited medtech businesses. Despite COVID, NATROX® is growing in South America and Asia, with significant success due in the US from Wound Care Clinics, Veteran Affairs and clinician sales.

description: LCC is a leading chemical technology company that manufacturers chemical building blocks called chiral components. Pharmaceutical companies use chiral components to create new compounds, which are needed to test and develop new drugs.
why_backed: LCC’s unique process routes and IP mean the company can create compounds that others cannot. LCC’s work also speeds up the drug development process, which can save pharmaceutical companies valuable time while making processes more efficient.

description: LightOx was founded by Carrie Ambler (CSO) and professor of Biosciences at Durham University and Dr Sam Whitehouse (CEO). The company is developing a treatment that will replace painful and highly invasive surgery or radiotherapy in patients with oral epithelial dysplasia (OED), a serious pre-cancerous condition affecting the mouth.
why_backed: OED affects 3% of the global population, but some treatments can be damaging to patients. For instance, cutting tissue from the mouth has been found to leave 95% of patients with life altering consequences, highlighting a clear need for LightOx’s first-in-class topical drug, which is activated by UV light.

description: Lunio’s technology specialises in tackling global ad fraud by combatting invalid and fraudulent traffic, which is usually caused by bots. Founded in 2018 by Neil Andrew, the Manchester-based business works with top global brands such as HUGO BOSS and M&S, enabling performance marketers to drive more commercial value and incremental success.
why_backed: Lunio’s research shows that one in 12 paid ad clicks are invalid, which translates to around $205bn in lost revenue opportunities in 2024 alone. This highlights the global scale of this issue as well as a growing addressable market for Lunio. The founder and CEO, Neil, has built a fantastic team and product, and the business is at the heart of a transformative period for ad and marketing tech.

description: Maxwellia is changing the face of medicine by switching prescription drugs to over the counter consumer products. Led by pharmacist Anna Maxwell, Maxwellia has recruited bright experts from GSK, Boots, J&J and Boehringer Ingelheim.
why_backed: Maxwellia’s impressive work helps GPs and pharmacies by empowering people to manage their everyday health. The team’s glowing track record now includes the launch of Lovima®, one of the first over the counter versions of the contraceptive pill.

description: Microlub, a University of Leeds spinout, has developed innovative technology to add lubrication to foods without increasing calorie content. The company’s unique protein and water scaffolds, coated by polysaccharides, make foods healthier and support the alternative protein industry. With strong traction among major food companies, Microlub aims to transform the market for reduced-fat and plant-based food products.
why_backed: Microlub’s technology addresses the global challenge of obesity by providing less-calorific alternatives without compromising taste. The company’s innovative approach has significant market potential, with strong traction among major food companies. Microlub’s commitment to making foods healthier and more sustainable also aligns with our reputation for supporting solutions that improve global health outcomes.

description: Modern Milkman is reimagining the milk round by connecting consumers with sustainable produce, including locally sourced dairy and fresh fruit and veg. Prioritising plastic-free packaging and reusable glass to reduce waste, Modern Milkman’s eco-friendly focus has also stopped over 50 million plastic bottles from entering the environment.
why_backed: Founded in 2018 by Simon Mellin, Modern Milkman has demonstrated headline-grabbing growth, earning it the title of 2022’s fastest-growing Northern tech company. Modern Milkman also utilises Peak AI’s Decision Intelligence platform to map out milk routes and assess demand, putting it at the cutting-edge of the grocery sector and aiding its expansion across the UK and Europe.

description: Mojo-CX, a Manchester-based SaaS business, leverages AI to analyse customer service conversations, train call handling staff, and enhance user experiences. Founded by CEO Jimmy Hosang in 2018, Mojo-CX offers three key tools: MO, JO, and CECE. These tools include an AI team leader, an agent assistant for analysing digital and voice conversations, and AI-driven analysis for fast and accessible insights.
why_backed: With more and more and business processes being transformed through AI, Mojo-CX stands out in its bid to improve and even progress the customer service experience with its smart tools. The company’s founder, Jimmy, is very backable and has identified a clear market gap for essential analytics, monitoring, and training tools.

description: OBT Live helps companies in media, sport, retail and leisure build brand loyalty and drive sales through bespoke digital experiences. The company specialises in LiveOps, the practice of dynamically updating digital environments to engage users, and uses its proprietary software (Engage AI) to create challenges, rewards and interactions.
why_backed: OBT Live is at the forefront of digital transformation. The company was founded by industry veterans who are well versed in using AI and data to take brands beyond static content. The company’s traction and rapid growth has also seen it expand into the Middle East, with a hub in Dubai and a global strategy to support brands worldwide.

description: Ocula is an innovative Retail Tech business that uses AI to optimise product pages at scale for online retailers and global brands. The company alleviates the largely manual process of updating product copy and optimising product pages for SEO by automating the process for its customer base, which includes major retailers in various sectors.
why_backed: Ocula performed significantly well during customer reference calls in the due diligence phase and demonstrated rapid growth in the lead up to our investment. The business is led by two very capable founders, and there is clear evidence of retailers increasing their conversion success as a result of using Ocula’s AI platform.

description: Outmin is an intelligent bookkeeping platform that uses artificial intelligence and automated data input to enable businesses to divert resource to higher value activities. Using Outmin’s platform, businesses report saving 200 hours annually on bookkeeping.
why_backed: As well as selling to businesses directly, Outmin has partnerships with a number of accounting practices, exposing the business to a growing audience. Our investment follows significant interest and investment in the finance sector, which is embracing AI and automation more and more.

description: Patchwork was founded to help ease the staffing crisis faced by the NHS and health sector. Working with 60 UK-wide NHS partners, Patchwork is bringing flexibility to staff and employers through its intuitive end-to-end workforce management offering.
why_backed: Patchwork is growing quickly and has a real opportunity to displace existing solutions across the entire NHS rostering space. The company’s founders, who are ex-doctors, are also closer to the problem they’re trying to solve than many others.

description: Peak specialises in Decision Intelligence, which is the commercial application of AI to grow profit and revenue. Peak’s approach combines complex data points with tailored AI to help brands like AO.com and PrettyLittleThing make better decisions.
why_backed: Peak has an incredible client base that stretches across multiple diverse industries. This includes FMCG giants like Pepsico and international retailers like Nike and ASOS, all of which are contributing to Peak’s world-class SaaS metrics.

description: Percayso is a data enrichment business which services the general insurance sector. Percayso’s next generation insurance intelligence adds further value to powerful datasets to prevent fraud, help insurers compete on price comparison sites and reduce risk levels.
why_backed: Percayso’s founder, Simon James, has already achieved great success in this space, having scaled and sold a similar company for £82m. Simon, who is well-known in the insurance space, still believes there is a major opportunity in the insurance data market, and has established Percayso to act as a competitor to his former business.

description: Pill Connect is a Manchester-based medtech company that has created an innovative digital device that attaches to pill bottles and tracks when a pill has been dispersed. The significance of this is Pill Connect can provide real-time dispensing data to pharmaceutical companies, therefore increasing the accuracy of clinical trials, which can sometimes be hampered by participants not taking the correct dosage of medicine or not within the guidelines set.
why_backed: Pill Connect’s technology addresses critical issues in clinical trials by ensuring correct patient compliance. The company’s partnerships with global leaders like Aardex and Aptar, along with its potential to aid vulnerable populations (e.g. the elderly or dementia patients), further highlight the impact the business can have outside of the clinical trial space.

description: Placed is a mobile-first and SaaS-based recruitment platform that connects employers with millennial and Gen Z talent. Instead of CVs, Placed matches candidates using questionnaires to assess job suitability. The platform also enables employers to post engaging content.
why_backed: Placed differentiates from the competition by enabling brands to interact, market and communicate with candidates within the platform. As brands are charged for access to the platform, there is a clear recurring revenue model. In addition, Placed already counts a number of major brands as clients, including E.On and Burger King.

description: RapidSpike’s award-winning website performance and security service interacts with sites via a consumer interface to better the digital experience. The company also alerts sites to cyber risks, user data theft and performance or reliability issues.
why_backed: RapidSpike’s clients include major names like William Hill, Matalan, Whittard of Chelsea and The Hut Group. RapidSpike is also the only solution of its kind focusing on performance, reliability and security, setting it apart in several growing and competitive digital sectors.

description: Reacta is modernising the process of testing for food allergies with what is believed to be the world’s first regulated and controlled oral food challenge. The result is a more effective and potentially safer test for undiagnosed individuals.
why_backed: The allergen market is global and growing, with clinical trials underway and new treatments incoming. Through its vital MHRA-approved work, Reacta has attracted a major pharmaceuticals contract and further opportunities are expected.

description: Re:course AI has been described as a flight simulator for the healthcare and life sciences industry. The technology trains clinicians by enabling them to interact with computer automated avatars, with real voices, instead of human patients. This enables clinicians to practise their approach and conversational delivery before entering the field.
why_backed: Re:course AI is putting safety and ethics at the heart of its development process, which has been welcomed by the healthcare community and investors alike. We invested because we believe the company has the potential to disrupt the healthcare and life sciences space, having already been integrated into healthcare institutions in the US and UK.

description: Ruuby has revolutionised the beauty industry by offering a seamless and user-friendly platform for on-demand beauty services. Since its inception, Ruuby has delivered nearly 500,000 services across multiple categories, including hair, nails, massage, waxing, IV drips, and cosmetic injectables.
why_backed: Ruuby is fast becoming a household name in beauty, with a long list of major businesses and known luxury brands as clients, including hotels. We also backed Ruuby on the basis of its commitment to continue its expansion into the North West, where it has already had prior success.

description: ScubaTx is a medtech company and Newcastle University spinout that has created a unique device to preserve donated organs and drive efficiencies in the organ transplant space. ScubaTx’s device utilises a technology called persufflation, which cools and oxygenates tissues with humidified gas at tightly controlled pressures and flow rates.
why_backed: Seatfrog has created a tech platform that enables rail passengers to easily upgrade their seat to first class or switch trains. The benefit to rail companies is the opportunity to increase margin on under-utilised first-class services and sell additional capacity. Through Seatfrog, passengers have saved more than £43m.

description: Seatfrog has created a tech platform that enables rail passengers to easily upgrade their seat to first class or switch trains. The benefit to rail companies is the opportunity to increase margin on under-utilised first-class services and sell additional capacity. Through Seatfrog, passengers have saved more than £43m.
why_backed: Seatfrog has exclusive long-term contracts of between 3 and 5 years with all UK rail operators, giving the company a level of exclusivity over 2,400 destinations. SF also integrates with each train operator’s backend, providing rail operators with key data and insights, which sets the company apart from companies like the Trainline. We also invested in Seatfrog on the back of strong customer feedback, with a 4.6/5 average rating from 17k reviews.

description: SiSU Health is an innovative healthcare platform focused on the prevention and early intervention of various health issues as well as addressing health inequalities. Through its unique health testing stations, which can be situated in places of work, worship and many other public settings, SiSU supports the early detection of risk factors such as high blood pressure and obesity. In addition, SiSU is encouraging healthier lifestyles and generating anonymised population health data for the NHS and other partners.
why_backed: Health inequality is of growing concern, with many demographics not accessing healthcare when it’s needed. We found SiSU Health’s approach to tackling this both backable and scalable. As well as placing devices in community settings, the company already working with a number of significant clients including Aldi, Jaguar, Land Rover, The AA and Workday, so that individuals can be tested against health markers at work, when it’s convenient for them, and without judgement.

description: Sparkbox uses AI and in-depth data to help big brand merchandising teams make better stock buying and pricing decisions. Trusted by major retailers such as River Island and Matchesfashion.com, their solution dramatically reduces waste and the need to heavily discount inventory.
why_backed: With 50 years’ worth of global retail experience between them, Sparkbox’s founders are well poised to modernise the stock and inventory world. Two of the founders, Lindsay and Matthew, are Forbes 30 under 30 inductees. Their co-founder Kevin was previously Vice President of Customer Insights at Best Buy and a retail analytics partner at Accenture.

description: Sprout AI is a claims automation engine, designed to automate the end-to-end claims process for high volume and typically low value insurance claims. By replacing human-led processes that are largely manual, slow and prone to error, Sprout helps to raise the customer experience, preventing high levels of customer churn.
why_backed: Sprout AI has long-term partnerships with three of the top ten global insurers (Axa, MetLife and Generali) and a management team with strong technical and commercial skills. We also identified Sprout as being an enterprise-level tech solution that is solving a significant problem for global insurers, with multiple machine learning models for high levels of accuracy.

description: SteamaCo is helping to transform the energy industry in Southeast Asia and Africa, where it provides advanced Internet of Things (IoT) technology to service both the on-grid and solar off-grid utility markets.
why_backed: COVID has meant setbacks for SteamaCo. But with a new focus on Nigeria’s grid sector, where theft costs utility companies $1.6bn a year, there is an opportunity for SteamaCo’s renewable energy expertise, particularly after the UN’s Climate report.

description: Sticky specialises in near field-communication technology in the form of customisable branded stickers which, when interacted with, enable customers to order and pay, virtually queue, donate and more. The company has also developed a low code/no code platform, enabling brands to maximise their outdoor retail space.
why_backed: We invested in Sticky on the strength of its self-serve backend platform, customer referencing and go to market partners, the calibre of which we seldom come across at this stage. This includes Elite Dynamics, which works with holiday parks, and WorldPay, which has access to large retail and hospitality opportunities worldwide. Other major clients include Costa Coffee and Byron Burger.

description: Street Group has created a range of cutting-edge tools for UK estate agents, aimed at helping the property sector become more efficient and customer-centric. Street’s offering is split across Street.co.uk – an innovative CRM with intelligent features – and Street Group’s all-in-one marketing solution Spectre which covers everything from automated direct mail campaigns to social media.
why_backed: Street Group is backed by a highly experienced founding team, with a strong background in real estate and a proven track record of building a successful business without external capital at the time of our investment. We believe Street Group is poised for continued growth and dominance in the sector.

description: Taveo (formerly Hubb) is a tech-enabled insurance broker, which targets the SME market by using a suite of technology tools, such as AI, to reduce the administration burden on brokers. Taveo also uses tech to reduce costs, improve efficiency and reduce human biases in a space that has seen little innovation to date.
why_backed: The Taveo team are focused on the industry’s shortfalls and the company’s highly backable founders have a clear vision of the industry’s future, which they see as being fully digitised through AI, automation and data science. These technologies enable Taveo to reduce SME insurance costs by 30% not to mention their ability to add transparency to process.

description: Tended is a Lincoln-based company that has developed a wearable safety solution to improve railway staff safety. The company’s geospatial positioning device alerts workers when they exit safe zones, helping them avoid hazards like open lines and heavy machinery.
why_backed: Tended’s solution significantly enhances the safety of railway staff by replacing outdated manual processes, such as verbal briefings and paper-based diagrams. The company works with Network Rail and Siemens Mobility and, at the time of our investment, has been expanding to Ireland, Northern Ireland and the Netherlands. Tended’s solution is also highly scalable, with plenty of potential for upsells.

description: The Padel Club is a fast-growing leisure club specialising in the popular racquet sport padel. Headquartered in Cheshire, it is the first business in the county to secure Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II) funding. The Padel Club is rapidly expanding with new nationwide facilities, taking the business far beyond its early successful beginnings in Wilmslow.
why_backed: The scale of The Padel Club’s ambitions (42 new courts by 2025) instantly impressed us, as did founder and CEO Kris Ball, whose background includes leading premium racquet and fitness clubs for over 14 years. The Padel Club’s facilities are immensely popular and the game is quickly becoming one of the fastest-growing sports in the UK, with a global fanbase that’s only growing.

description: TransReport is a SaaS company that helps transport providers monitor, facilitate and act on passenger feedback more efficiently. The company covers all areas of transport, including the rail sector, where it has several long-term contracts.
why_backed: TransReport’s early success has led to a contract from National Rail to roll out its Passenger Assistance app, which serves disabled passengers. This news, and the company’s scope to take on Europe and other travel sectors, is very exciting.

description: WatchMyCompetitor (WMC) uses cutting-edge artificial intelligence to monitor competitors, clients, regulators and key partners, making the process of scraping and obtaining crucial data simple and intuitive. This enables marketing, product and sales teams to respond to real-time developments.
why_backed: WMC was born out of a real-life business need and is already attracting global customers in multiple sectors, all of which often have to be across multiple channels at once. WMC’s platform delivers what every management team needs to make the best decisions – the right information in real time.

description: wi-Q is a SaaS business that specialises in innovative mobile ordering and payment solutions, which give customers the ability to order food, drinks and other services from their mobile, quickly and easily. These solutions are used by a broad range of hospitality clients, including the world’s top hotel chains. wi-Q also works with home delivery brands and fast casual dining restaurants.
why_backed: In addition to wi-Q’s work with a number of major hospitality brands, we were impressed by the company’s backable CEO and senior leadership team as well as its expansion plans, which include growth in the US and Asia-Pacific regions. Mobile ordering technology, including that offered by wi-Q has also become the norm post-covid, with the sector expected to surpass £159bn in the next several years.

description: XR Games is vying to become the leading games developer in the AR/VR gaming space. XR’s titles, including The Angry Birds Movie 2 VR: Under Pressure and Zombieland: Headshot Fever, have garnered critical acclaim and praise from giants like Sony.
why_backed: XR Games has earned a reputation for developing blockbuster games, with a client list that includes Sony, Rovio, Dreamworks, BBC and Lego. XR’s team also boasts big-game experience from major studios like Rockstar, EA, Codemasters and Sumo.
